The agriculturalcycle encompasses the sequence of activities involved in the production of
crops, from the initial planting and cultivation to the subsequent harvesting and preparation
for consumption or sale. In the context of wheat cultivation in Uppsala, Sweden, the annual
agricultural cycle is characterized by the singular occurrence of a single cycle specifically
dedicated to winter wheat cultivation. This is primarily attributable to the prevailing cold
climatic conditions that are characteristic of northern Europe. The cycle commences with
the sowing of seeds in September, followed by the harvesting of the crop in May of the
subsequent year. Consequently, during the four-month interval from May to September, the
biomass of wheat in the food web is negligible.

Concurrently, the season exerts a substantial influence on the growth of wheat. During win-
ter, temperatures are lower, and wheat enters the overwintering period. Warm winters have
been observed to increase the prevalence of disease and insect sources in wheat fields, in-
ducing insect pests. Conversely, cold winters have been shown to lead to frost damage to
wheat and the phenomenon of dead stems and seedlings. Consequently, the period from
